answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small collateral bond, locked at the dawn of its first trade and released only after a history of verified work. Peers view that history through a prism of independent attestations: a new identity with no endorsements gets near-zero trust, while an established one earns higher limits. Faking many identities means funding many bonds and waiting out the same slow history for each, and if one copies another's work, its record turns umber, flagged and slashed, so the attack costs more than any gain from duplicate votes.
